claim_verdicts.evidence: Scoped: "Register scoped services by calling AddScoped." Registration table: `Add{LIFETIME}<{SERVICE}, {IMPLEMENTATION}>()` and `Add{LIFETIME}<{IMPLEMENTATION}>()`. "Registering a service with only an implementation type is equivalent to registering that service with the same implementation and service type."

"Beginning with C# 14, there are two syntaxes you use to define extension methods. C# 14 adds extension blocks... Before C# 14, you add the this modifier to the first parameter of a static method" "Both forms of extensions must be defined inside a non-nested, nongeneric static class." Pinned lang is C# 14, so the §3 definition describes only one of two forms; also omits the static-class requirement.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: extension method — a static method, in a static class, that can be called as if it belonged to another type. The form Đơn Hàng uses marks its first parameter with `this`, so `AddDonHangInfrastructure(this IServiceCollection services, ...)` can be called as `builder.Services.AddDonHangInfrastructure(...)`.

claim_verdicts.evidence: EF Core provider table: "PostgreSQL* | `.UseNpgsql(connectionString)` | Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL". DonHang.Infrastructure.csproj references Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL (10.0.3 per versions.yaml).

Claim as written (constructor injection throws, never injects null) holds: scratch app (net10.0, WebApplication.CreateBuilder + AddControllers, SDK 10.0.300) printed `InvalidOperationException: Unable to resolve service for type 'Svc' while attempting to activate 'TController'.` But the same run printed `GetService<Svc> null? True`: IServiceProvider.GetService returns null for an unregistered type, so lesson §4 "the container never answers with `null`" and §9 "never return `null`" are too broad.
claim_verdicts.source: scratch app (net10.0, WebApplication.CreateBuilder + AddControllers, SDK 10.0.300); refs/aspnetcore-docs/aspnetcore/fundamentals/app-state.md:270 (same message format)
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A registration can be missing, and the container never fills a constructor parameter with `null`. When it cannot find a registration for a type a constructor asks for, it throws an exception naming that type.

claim_verdicts.evidence: "in the development environment, ValidateOnBuild and ValidateScopes are enabled." (.NET 9 change, still in force). scratch app (net10.0, WebApplication.CreateBuilder + AddControllers, SDK 10.0.300) with ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development and INotifier removed: `BUILD FAIL: AggregateException: Some services are not able to be constructed (... Unable to resolve service for type 'INotifier' while attempting to activate 'Svc'.)`; Production: `BUILD OK`. docker-compose.yml:93 `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: "Development"`.

"By default, ASP.NET Core doesn't register controllers as services in the DI container. The runtime uses the DefaultControllerActivator to create controller instances and resolves services from the DI container for constructor parameters". Scratch app, Development, Svc unregistered: `BUILD OK`, then GET → `InvalidOperationException ... activate 'TController'` → 500. ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs catch (Exception) writes 500 (InvalidOperationException is not KeyNotFound/Argument).

OrdersController.cs:12 `OrdersController(OrderService orderService, IOrderRepository repository)`; OrderService.cs `OrderService(IOrderRepository repository, INotifier notifier)`; ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:15 is the only IOrderRepository registration (git grep at stage-1). Scratch app: controller and Svc both resolved IRepo from one AddScoped line (GET → 200).

Follows from the code: the only INotifier registration is ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:16 and Program.cs names no notifier. Holds on the condition that the new class's constructor needs only types already registered (see minor issue on §7).

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and false for this repo: DonHang.Api also uses EF Core directly. Program.cs:7 `using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;` and :61 `context.Database.Migrate();`; ProductsController uses `ToListAsync`, AuthController `FirstOrDefaultAsync` (both `using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;`). Infrastructure is the project that holds the EF Core package reference, not the only one that knows about EF Core.
issues.quote: the one project that knows about EF Core
issues.fix: Replace the clause with: "which class answers `IOrderRepository` is decided inside `DonHang.Infrastructure`, next to `EfOrderRepository` and `LoggingNotifier` themselves." Do not add a claim about EF Core being confined to one project.

issues.text: Overbroad: IServiceProvider.GetService returns null for an unregistered type (scratch app: `GetService<Svc> null? True`). Only constructor injection / GetRequiredService throws. Same overstatement in §9 line 5 and quiz q2/q4 explanations ("never hands out `null` for a missing registration").
issues.quote: A registration can be missing, and the container never answers with `null`.
issues.fix: Use claim 6 suggested_text in §4. §9 line 5: "A missing registration makes the container throw when it builds a constructor, at startup or on the first request that needs it; it never passes `null` in." q2 correct-explanation: "The container never passes `null` into a constructor for a missing registration."

issues.fix: Add a claim (kind behavior, version_key efcore, section 4): "AddDbContext registers the DbContext type with a scoped lifetime by default", source refs/efcore-docs/entity-framework/core/dbcontext-configuration/index.md:419. No text change needed.

issues.fix: Use claim 4 suggested_text (says "the form Đơn Hàng uses" and "in a static class"). Do not introduce extension blocks.
